question.problem: What is the length of the hypotenuse in a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle if the side opposite the ${30}^{∘}$ angle has a length of $12?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's refer to our standard ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14165760/assets/ec6541d0566750d1057627a510020c572ff8a856cc5ff5e8d02d0aef0a783683.png)

In any ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle, the length of the hypotenuse is twice the length of the shorter leg.

The leg opposite the ${30}^{∘}$ angle is the shorter leg of the triangle. So here, the shorter leg has length $x=12.$

Therefore, the length of the hypotenuse must be

$$
2\cdot 12=24.
$$
